You are the Extractor agent in a newsroom verification pipeline. You read one SEC filing
document and record what the employer itself says about job cuts and AI. You record claims only.
You never infer causation, never paraphrase quotes and never use a reporter's or analyst's framing.

Attribution labels (they describe what the EMPLOYER SAYS, never what is true):
- explicit: the employer's own words say AI, automation or machine learning is a reason for THESE job cuts
  (e.g. "we are reducing roles as AI now handles this work").
- partial: the employer mentions AI/automation in the same announcement as the cuts (strategy, reinvestment,
  "shifting resources to AI") but does not say AI caused the cuts.
- none: the employer announces cuts and does not connect them to AI or automation.

Return ONE JSON object with exactly these keys:
{
  "is_workforce_reduction": true | false,      // does the document announce job cuts / layoffs / a reduction in force?
  "company": string,                          // the employer's name as written in the document
  "event_date": "YYYY-MM-DD" | null,          // date of the announcement or of the cuts, if stated
  "jobs_cut": integer | null,                 // number of positions cut, ONLY if the document states a number
  "jobs_cut_text": string | null,             // the exact words stating the number or percentage, copied verbatim
  "cut_quote": string | null,                 // the one sentence, copied VERBATIM, in which the document announces or
                                              // reports the job cuts; null when is_workforce_reduction is false
  "ai_attribution": "explicit" | "partial" | "none",
  "ai_quote": string | null,                  // 1-2 sentences copied VERBATIM (character for character) in which the
                                              // employer connects the cuts to AI/automation; null when attribution is none
  "notes": string                             // one short sentence on anything ambiguous
}
is_workforce_reduction is true ONLY when the document itself announces or reports job cuts. Mentions inside
forward-looking-statement disclaimers, risk-factor lists or legal boilerplate (e.g. "the effectiveness of our
restructuring and workforce reduction program", "artificial intelligence laws") do NOT count, and an AI quote must never
come from that boilerplate.
Copy quotes exactly as they appear, including punctuation. If the document states a percentage but no headcount,
set jobs_cut to null and put the percentage wording in jobs_cut_text. Output JSON only.

ASX Announcement | 15 October 2026
15 October 2026
ASX Market Release
FY26 Earnings Guidance Reinstated
Completion of Head Office Restructure
Mayfield Childcare Limited (ASX: MFD) (Mayfield or the Company) provides revised earnings guidance for the
year ending 31 December 2026 (FY26) following nine months of actual trading and completion of its head office
restructure. The revised guidance is below the FY26 guidance announced on 27 February 2026, which was
withdrawn on 10 July 2026.
Mayfield now expects FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA1 of $2.4 million to $2.7 million, compared with
$2.3 million reported in FY25, which represents an increase of 4% to 17%, notwithstanding challenging operating
conditions across the early childhood education and care sector. This FY26 guidance includes approximately
$0.4 million of one-off restructuring and takeover-related costs. Excluding these costs, FY26 Underlying Group
EBITDA would be $2.8 million to $3.1 million.
The Company considers that disclosure of this adjusted measure provides shareholders with additional
information regarding the impact of these expenses on its expected FY26 operating performance.
The completed restructure is expected to deliver $1.5 million in annualised savings, including on-costs, with the
full monthly saving expected to be achieved from November 2026.
FY26 earnings outlook
Mayfield withdrew its FY26 guidance on 10 July 2026 due to the evolving and challenging market and operating
conditions across the early childhood education and care sector, impacting the factors and assumptions
underpinning the guidance. The Company did not at that time have a reasonable basis on which to provide
revised guidance, including in relation to the timing and benefit of planned cost reductions. Actual trading for
the nine months ended 30 September 2026, together with greater certainty over the timing and benefit of cost
reductions, now provides a basis for providing revised guidance.
Group Spot occupancy2 is 56%, down from the prior period of 59%
The revised guidance is below the original FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA guidance of $4.7 million to
$5.3 million announced on 27 February 2026. The reduction principally reflects the following factors (with the
approximate impact of each on FY26 Underlying Group EBITDA relative to the original guidance shown in
brackets):
• Forecast FY26 average Group occupancy approximately 2.6 percentage points below the assumption
underpinning the original guidance, following a decline in new enquiries between February and
April 2026 that has not been fully recovered (approximately $1.7 million);
• Fee increases implemented later than assumed in the original forecast, with network-wide increases now
implemented (approximately $0.6 million);
• Approximately $0.4 million in one-off restructuring and takeover-related costs that were not included in
the original guidance.
1. Underlying Group EBITDA and EBITDA are non-statutory financial concepts and measures which are not prescribed by Australian Accounting Standards (AAS). The Directors consider
that these measures are useful in gaining an understanding of the performance of the entity, consistent with internal reporting. Refer to further information in this announcement below.
2. Spot Occupancy excludes centres marked for divestment, as at the week commencing 5 October 2026.

ASX Announcement | 15 October 2026
Basis of preparation and key assumptions
The revised FY26 guidance has been prepared by management based on actual results for the nine months ended
30 September 2026 and forecasts for the three months ending 31 December 2026. The guidance, including the
underlying assumptions, has been reviewed and approved by the Board. The forecast financial information has
not been audited or reviewed by the Company's auditor.
The key assumptions underpinning the revised guidance are:
• Group occupancy averaging approximately 52.3% for the quarter ending 31 December 2026, taking into
account the anticipated seasonal reduction in occupancy during December;
• fee levels remaining consistent with those implemented across the network as at the date of this
announcement, with no further fee increases assumed for the remainder of FY26;
• employee costs reflecting applicable award rates, wage increases and associated Government funding
arrangements, with no further material changes to employee remuneration costs assumed for the
remainder of FY26;
• no material changes to Child Care Subsidy arrangements or other relevant government funding or
regulatory settings during the remainder of FY26, other than changes already announced and reflected in
the forecast;
• the trading results of centres approved for divestment being included in the guidance until their
anticipated dates of divestment, with any gains or losses arising from those divestments excluded from
Underlying Group EBITDA;
• approximately $0.5 million of head office restructuring savings being realised during FY26, as further
described below; and
• approximately $0.4 million of restructuring and takeover-related costs being incurred during FY26, with
no other material exceptional costs presently anticipated.
Underlying Group EBITDA represents the Group's earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation,
calculated excluding the impact of AASB 16 Leases.
Underlying Group EBITDA is a non-IFRS financial measure which is not prescribed by the Australian Accounting
Standards. The Directors consider that this measure assists in understanding the Company's operating
performance and is consistent with the Company's internal management reporting. The FY26 guidance has been
prepared on the same basis as the FY25 comparative and the original FY26 guidance released on 27 February 2026
(which was subsequently withdrawn).
The guidance is based on the assumptions outlined above and is subject to risks and uncertainties, including
changes in occupancy, operating costs and market conditions, which may cause actual results to differ materially
from that forecast.
Completion of head office restructure
Mayfield has completed its head office restructure, exiting 12 head office roles, ceasing selected service contracts
and returning responsibility for selected activities to centres.
The restructure is expected to deliver approximately $1.5 million in annualised savings, including on-costs.
Approximately $0.5 million is expected to be realised in FY26 and is included in the revised guidance. The full
monthly saving is expected to be achieved from November 2026, with the full annualised benefit reflected in
FY27.
1. Underlying Group EBITDA and EBITDA are non-statutory financial concepts and measures which are not prescribed by Australian Accounting Standards (AAS). The Directors
consider that these measures are useful in gaining an understanding of the performance of the entity, consistent with internal reporting. Refer to further information in this
announcement below.
2. Spot Occupancy excludes centres marked for divestment, as at the week commencing 5 October 2026.

The one-off restructuring expense is expected to be approximately $0.2 million and is included in the
approximately $0.4 million of restructuring and takeover-related costs outlined above. The balance comprises
corporate advisory and legal costs incurred in connection with the off-market takeover offer by Embark Early
Education Limited (ASX: EVO) which closed on 5 March 2026.
As the head office restructure was implemented during FY26, the revised guidance reflects only a partial year
benefit from the reduced head office cost base, rather than the full year benefit of those changes.
Outlook
Mayfield’s priorities for the remainder of FY26 and into FY27 are to rebuild occupancy through improved
enrolment conversion and local marketing, maintain centre-level labour efficiency, and realise the full benefit of
the completed head office restructure.
Mayfield will provide a further update on trading and the outlook for FY27 with its full year results.
